items.item: ISA-95's levels are a functional model sorted by time horizon, not an org chart or a network diagram — the same function can in principle run on different hardware at different plants and still sit at the same level.

items.item: The standard's own page is explicit that it "primarily deals with the interface between levels 3 and 4" — the levels below that boundary are named but not the standard's main subject matter.

items.item: The SCADA-at-level-2-vs-level-3 disagreement is exactly the kind of surface disagreement that collapses once you ask the right question: not 'which box is SCADA' but 'what time horizon does this activity operate on'.

at.step: Reveal: the SCADA naming trap

items.item: A hierarchy dimension's grain has to be (equipment, time), not just (equipment) — treating it as a pure lookup table with no valid-time window is the single most common SCD mistake, and it is invisible until something actually moves.

at.step: Reveal: the hierarchy as a type-2 SCD, keyed durably

items.item: A type-2 SCD row's surrogate key identifies a version of the equipment's state, not the equipment itself — two rows for the same physical machine is the model working correctly, not a duplicate to be deduplicated.

at.step: Reveal: the hierarchy as a type-2 SCD, keyed durably

items.item: The join bug this topic measures doesn't require a stale table at all — even a hierarchy table updated the instant a machine moves will mis-answer any historical question unless the join itself carries the event's own timestamp into the lookup.

at.step: Reveal: the measured join bug

items.item: The understatement on one line and the overstatement on the other are the same number by construction: the join bug doesn't destroy or create output, it only relocates one equipment's entire pre-move total onto the wrong line.

at.step: Reveal: the measured join bug

items.item: A surrogate key existing per SCD row (not per physical machine) is a feature, not an accident: it's what lets the dimension carry two different, mutually exclusive 'truths' about the same equipment_id without contradiction.

at.step: Reveal: why equipment_id or a tag name can't carry this alone

items.item: A tag name or equipment_id answers 'which machine', never 'which machine, as of when' — the second question is exactly what a line or location attribute can't answer by itself once that attribute can change.

at.step: Reveal: why equipment_id or a tag name can't carry this alone

items.item: Every later topic in this chapter that joins to 'the hierarchy' (production entities, quality, OEE, energy) inherits this exact as-of requirement; topic 1's bug is the chapter's recurring failure mode, not a one-off.

A 'current state' cache (the Prove-it scenario) reintroduces the identical bug in a new disguise: refreshing it faster narrows the window where it's wrong, but never closes the window to zero unless the lookup itself carries event time.
